content: 1. Lamivudine and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) are indicated for use in combination with other antiretroviral agents for the treatment of HIV-1 infection. The recommended dosage is one tablet containing lamivudine 300 mg and tenofovir 300 mg, taken orally once daily in combination with other antiretroviral therapies (ARTs). 2. Clinical trials have not included a sufficient number of patients aged 65 years or older to determine whether they respond differently from younger individuals. Caution should be exercised when administering lamivudine to elderly patients due to the higher likelihood of decreased hepatic, renal, or cardiac function, as well as the presence of concomitant diseases or other drug therapies. 3. The combination of lamivudine and elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir is contraindicated. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be co-administered with other antiretroviral agents. Additionally, both emtricitabine and lamivudine increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome, and their co-administration should be avoided due to therapeutic duplication. 4. Co-administration of lamivudine-containing products with emtricitabine-containing products is contraindicated. This combination results in therapeutic duplication and should be avoided. 5. Antiretroviral medications, including lamivudine, may interfere with the manufacturing of autologous cell-based therapies such as atidarsagene autotemcel, betibeglogene autotemcel, and lovotibeglogene autotemcel. Patients should discontinue antiretroviral therapy at least one month before cell mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period for complete elimination. 6. Sorbitol-containing solutions decrease the systemic exposure of lamivudine oral solution, as demonstrated in pediatric studies (e.g., the ARROW trial). This results in lower rates of virologic suppression, reduced plasma lamivudine levels, and increased development of viral resistance compared to children receiving lamivudine tablets. Co-administration with sorbitol should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 7. Tafenoquine increases the levels or effects of lamivudine by inhibiting organic cation transporter-2 (OCT2) and multidrug and toxin extrusion (MATE) transporters. Co-administration with OCT2 or MATE substrates should be avoided. If unavoidable, monitor for substrate-related toxicities and consider dosage adjustments based on product labeling. 8. Trilaciclib decreases the levels or effects of lamivudine by inhibiting OCT2, MATE1, and MATE-2K transporters. Co-administration should be avoided, especially with substrates where even minimal increases in concentration could lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. 9. Lamivudine increases the levels of cabozantinib by inhibiting multidrug resistance-associated protein 2 (MRP2). This increases the risk of cabozantinib toxicity. Use caution, monitor closely, and consider alternative therapies or dose adjustments. 10. Co-administration of lamivudine with ribavirin increases the risk of lactic acidosis due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Alternatives should be considered if available. 11. Lamivudine and zidovudine exhibit beneficial pharmacodynamic synergism, but both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Lamivudine and atazanavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Lamivudine and efavirenz both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Lamivudine and ritonavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Lamivudine and fosamprenavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Lamivudine and indinavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Lamivudine and nevirapine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Lamivudine and enfuvirtide both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Lamivudine and ganciclovir increase the risk of hematologic toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 20. Lamivudine and valganciclovir increase the risk of hematologic toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Alternatives should be considered if available. 21. Lamivudine and interferon alfa-2b increase the risk of liver decompensation due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Lamivudine and peginterferon alfa-2a increase the risk of liver decompensation due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Lamivudine and peginterferon alfa-2b increase the risk of liver decompensation due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of lamivudine by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 25. Isavuconazonium sulfate, an OCT2 inhibitor, may increase the effects or levels of lamivudine. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 26. Trimethoprim increases the effects of lamivudine by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor for potential toxicity. 27. Ublituximab decreases the effects of lamivudine due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 28. Orlistat decreases the levels or effects of lamivudine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and if an increased viral load is confirmed, discontinue orlistat. 29. Givinostat, a weak OAT2 inhibitor, increases the levels or effects of lamivudine. Close monitoring is required, especially when co-administered with OCT2-sensitive substrates where small changes in plasma concentration may lead to serious toxicities.
